business.claim: Canva is an online design and publishing tool launched in 2013, with the mission of empowering everyone to design anything and publish anywhere.
Canva uses a freemium/subscription model: Free, paid Pro and Business plans, and custom-priced Enterprise; paid tiers add premium creation, storage, AI and collaboration features.
The Visual Suite combines Docs, Emails, Sheets, Whiteboards, Presentations, Social, Video, Websites and landing pages in a collaborative workspace with Canva AI embedded across workflows.
Canva serves individuals, creators, small businesses, educators, nonprofits, teams and large enterprises; the company says K-12 organizations and nonprofits can access most premium features for free.
Canva operates globally in 190+ countries and 100+ languages, with localization through local templates, elements, payment methods and partnerships.
Canva Enterprise is positioned for large organizations needing centralized brand control, administration, reporting, security, collaboration and integrations.

traction.claim: Company claim: Canva reported 260 million monthly users and $3.5 billion in revenue in 2025.

Company claim reported by TechCrunch: Canva ended 2025 with more than 265 million monthly active users, over 31 million paid users and $4 billion in ARR; its business serving companies with more than 25 seats reached $500 million ARR after 100% growth.
Company claim: Canva says it is used by 95% of the Fortune 500 and by thousands of companies through Canva Enterprise.
Named Enterprise customers include FedEx, Keller Williams and DocuSign; Canva reported FedEx deployment across 1,400 teams in 45 countries and DocuSign savings of $300,000 in design hours.
Company claim: 100 million teachers, students and education leaders used Canva monthly in 2025 across 190+ countries.
Canva said it added more than 700,000 non-English templates and 2.3 million local elements in six months; in Japan it partnered with Irasutoya to add over 20,000 illustrations.
Canva's Salesforce case study claims use across 140+ social accounts, 22 regions and 18 languages, with a 63% increase in design production and 66% lower cost per design.

team.claim: Canva's founding team is Melanie Perkins (CEO), Cliff Obrecht (COO) and Cameron Adams (Chief Product Officer).
Before Canva, Perkins and Obrecht built Fusion Books, an online school-yearbook design business; Cameron Adams joined as the technology co-founder after an introduction facilitated by Lars Rasmussen.
Kelly Steckelberg joined Canva as CFO in November 2024 after serving as Zoom CFO; before Zoom she held finance roles at Cisco and was CEO of Zoosk.
Javier Soltero left Canva's operating enterprise role in May 2024 after about six months and returned to an adviser role; he previously held senior roles at Google and Microsoft.
Canva's official newsroom identifies Cameron Adams as co-founder and Chief Product Officer and describes his earlier work with Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht on the Canva idea.

funding.claim: Canva announced a $15 million Series A in October 2015, led by Felicis Ventures with Blackbird Ventures and Matrix Partners participating, at a $165 million valuation.
Canva raised another $15 million in September 2016 in a round led by Blackbird Ventures and Felicis Ventures, taking valuation to $345 million.
Canva announced a $40 million round in January 2018 at a $1 billion valuation; Sequoia China joined Blackbird and Felicis, and Canva said Blackbird partner Rick Baker led the round.

Canva raised $70 million in May 2019 at a $2.5 billion valuation, followed by an $85 million round in October 2019 that lifted valuation to $3.2 billion; investors included Bond, General Catalyst, Bessemer, Blackbird and Sequoia China.
Canva announced a $60 million round in June 2020, taking valuation to $6 billion; the announcement quoted Bond and Blackbird investors but did not identify a single lead investor.

Canva announced a $200 million funding round on September 15, 2021, led by T. Rowe Price at a $40 billion valuation; participants included Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree.

Canva launched an employee stock sale in August 2025 at a $42 billion valuation; Reuters reported Fidelity Management led and JPMorgan Asset Management joined, with share count undisclosed. This was a secondary employee-liquidity transaction rather than a disclosed primary capital raise.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim: Canva reported $3.5 billion in 2025 revenue and 260 million monthly users.

Company statement reported by TechCrunch: Canva ended 2025 with $4 billion ARR, more than 265 million monthly active users and over 31 million paid users; B2B ARR reached $500 million after 100% growth.
Reuters reported Canva's annualized revenue at $3.3 billion during the 2025 employee share sale.

Reported filing data: FY2022 revenue rose 57% to $962 million; Canva posted a $222 million statutory loss driven largely by $482 million of employee-benefit expense, while cash reserves rose to $420 million. Excluding share-based payments, the source says the company made a $260 million profit.
Company claim reported by Startup Daily: Canva says it has been profitable on an operating free-cash-flow basis for several years and had surpassed $3.4 billion in annualized revenue.
Canva had more than 5,000 staff worldwide and reportedly added about 1,000 employees in 2024.

Reported workforce reduction: 10 of Canva's 12 technical-writing staff were made redundant in late March 2025; Canva described the change as engineers taking greater ownership of documentation with new tools, while the report linked it to an AI-intensive workflow shift.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: ASIC issued A$792,000 in infringement notices to four Australian Canva Group companies for allegedly failing to lodge FY2024 financial reports by the 30 April 2025 deadline; each paid A$198,000. ASIC states payment is not an admission of liability or a conviction.

A CourtListener federal docket lists DigiMedia Tech, LLC v. Canva Pty Ltd, an E.D. Texas patent-infringement action filed August 18, 2025; the docket was not shown as terminated in the retrieved record.

Canva disclosed a May 24, 2019 security incident in which profile-database information for up to 139 million users was accessed; it said partial payment-card files were viewed but found no evidence they were stolen, and it reset OAuth tokens and prompted password changes.
Canva later said approximately 4 million passwords from the 2019 incident had been decrypted and shared online, and it reset passwords that users had not changed.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor showed Canva at 3.8/5 from 904 reviews, with 86% CEO approval and 61% positive business outlook; category scores were stronger for diversity and inclusion (4.1) and weaker for senior management (3.1) and career opportunities (3.1).

Recent Glassdoor reviews were mixed: a May 2026 former employee praised coworkers and the product but alleged leadership and churn problems, while a January 2026 current employee review cited low ownership and inconsistent decision-making; these are anonymous allegations.

Indeed displayed an overall Canva rating of 4.3/5 based on 32 reviews, with 3.7/5 for pay and benefits and job security/advancement; the sample is small and includes both positive and negative comments.
BBB's Canva complaints page showed 171 complaints in the last three years and 77 in the last 12 months; the page warns that displayed complaints may not represent all complaints.

Trustpilot showed Canva at 4.0/5 from 7,884 reviews; its platform-generated summary was positive on ease of use but cited recurring criticism of unintuitive editing, customer-support response times and print alignment.

Fox Business reported customer backlash to Canva Teams price increases in September 2024, including examples of annual pricing rising from $119.99 to $300 and then $500; Canva said the change reflected expanded product experience and tools.

People Matters reported that the technical-writer cuts unsettled employees who said they had been encouraged to adopt AI and reassured it would not cause layoffs; this is critical reporting, not an adjudicated finding.

red_flags.claim: Late financial reporting: ASIC said four Canva Group entities missed the FY2024 filing deadline and paid A$792,000 in infringement notices, although ASIC said payment was not an admission of liability or a conviction.
Cybersecurity overhang: Canva's own incident FAQ says profile data for up to 139 million users was accessed in 2019 and about 4 million passwords were later decrypted and shared online.

Workforce and culture risk: reporting described the elimination of 10 of 12 technical-writing roles amid an AI workflow shift, while employee-review snapshots cited weaker scores for management and career opportunities.

Monetization/reputation risk: customer complaints and critical coverage followed large Canva Teams price increases, with BBB recording 171 complaints over three years and Trustpilot reviewers citing support and subscription-related issues.

Valuation risk: Forbes Australia reported that investor marks in 2026 had been reduced from the $42 billion 2025 valuation, including Blackbird's mark to $34.9 billion and T. Rowe Price's implied valuation to $38.2 billion.

output.verdict: Canva shows unusually strong scale and product traction for a private software company: large and growing monthly reach, paid-user and B2B ARR growth, broad international distribution, Fortune 500 penetration, and a credible founder/CFO bench. The closer look should focus on the quality and reconciliation of company-reported revenue versus ARR, the implications of AI cost and workforce changes, the 2026 valuation marks versus the 2025 secondary, filing-governance discipline, and the residual security/reputation liabilities.
